meaning:
ξηρός, -ά, -όν
[in LXX chiefly for יָבֵשׁ, its parts and deriva­tives, also for חָרָבָה, etc. ;]
dry: metaphorically (of a sinner), ξύλον ξ., Luk.23:31; of members of the body shrunken by disease, withered: Jhn.5:3; of the hand, Mat.12:10 Mrk.3:3, Luk.6:6, 8; of the dry land, ἡ ξηρά (sc. γῆ, cf. Gen.1:9-10; Jon.1:19, al.): Mat.23:15; γῆ, Heb.11:29.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: And behold there was a man with a withered hand. They asked him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath day?” that they might accuse him.
He said to the man who had his hand withered, “Stand up.”
It also happened on another Sabbath that he entered into the synagogue and taught. There was a man there, and his right hand was withered.
In these lay a great multitude of those who were sick, blind, lame, or paralyzed, waiting for the moving of the water;
By faith, they passed through the Red Sea as on dry land. When the Egyptians tried to do so, they were swallowed up.
